description: Fork of exp724 (E=384, NAP-bump, hybrid_smooth K-row dense backward = 1.1936 @ 276.83M). Replaces each LUT module's forward call with a custom torch.autograd.Function (`_AsymFn` in train.py) that: forward = 2-row blend (main + Hamming-1 alt at argmin|d|, weighted by u — identical to exp724's forward); backward input gradient = (NAP+1)-row softmax over the full Hamming-1 ball (main + all NAP single-bit-flip neighbors). Weight gradient is 2-row scatter (consistent with forward output). T_sel/T_soft gradients flow through the (NAP+1)-row softmax path. This is the asymmetric mode neither exp724 (2-fwd, K-row bwd) nor exp726 (NAP+1-fwd, NAP+1-bwd) provides: it keeps forward cheap (2 rows) AND backward FLOP-bounded (NAP+1 rows) instead of dense K-row. Comparison anchors: exp724=1.1936 (2-fwd, K-bwd); exp726=1.1997 (NAP+1-fwd, NAP+1-bwd); exp727=trailing badly (2-fwd, 2-bwd).
